capture_source: live capture 2026-09-01; SAP A4H kernel 793 over WebSocket RFC at /sap/bc/rfc. Reply to a wRFC LOGON carrying an embedded RFCPING with an EMPTY ngrfc body. Sanitised: the 0x0418 breadcrumb's P= hex blob is zeroed and the user name replaced, both length-preserving, so every TLV offset stays valid.
evidence: the same 1118-byte reply arrived on three separate connections in one probe run, in 48-1051 ms; a LOGON with ngrfc body b'\\x45' instead draws no reply at all for 30 s

expected_parse.error_text: Error when receiving data for an RFC.

notes: This reply is BOTH an authentication success and a function-call failure. 0x0450-0x0453 carry the system identity and are filled in regardless of whether the call embedded in the LOGON ran. A reader that checks only for a sys_id sees a clean logon, which is exactly what the library did: it declared the session ready, sent an invoke into it, and the work process took a short dump -- returned as a WebSocket close with reason 'RABAX_STATE:Error when receiving data for an RFC.'

0x0418 is the ABAP call-stack breadcrumb: ';W=SAPLSYSU,E=163,H=3,N=3;S=RFCPING,P=SAPLSYSU;S=WEBRFCCALL,P=SAPWEBRFC;...'. The E=163 in it is where the number in issue #14 comes from. It was hardcoded in two places and used as a fallback in a third rather than read from here -- a constant that happens to be right is still wrong, because it reports 163 for failures that are not 163.

The failure itself is honest: an empty ngrfc body means the embedded RFCPING receives no data, and 'Error when receiving data for an RFC' describes that exactly. What a correct LOGON-embedded body looks like is still open -- b'\\x45', which makes the 0x5001 record byte-identical to a working INVOKE, leaves the server silent indefinitely.
0x0416 is 'X' (message type X = short dump / abort) and 0x0417 is '341', the same message number as signon_incomplete_752_response.bin, which is also class 00 type X.
